Trap findings: TSQL-01, TSQL-02, TSQL-04, TSQL-05, TSQL-13, TSQL-16
Trap cards for the suspected traps:
### TSQL-01: Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins
Legacy: Under a case-insensitive collation such as SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text compares equal regardless of letter case (and of trailing spaces, see TSQL-02): state = 'ACTIVE' also matches 'Active' and 'active'; GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and join keys put case variants together. The stored value is returned unchanged.
Spark: Spark compares strings in binary order: 'Active' <> 'ACTIVE', so a filter drops case variants, a GROUP BY splits them into separate groups and a join misses them.
Fix: Compare, group, partition and join on upper(rtrim(x)) (or collate(x, 'UTF8_LCASE_RTRIM')) while selecting the original column for output. Never change the stored value unless the legacy code does (e.g. UPPER in the SELECT). Use rtrim, not trim: leading spaces count.
### TSQL-02: Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces
Legacy: SQL Server pads the shorter string with spaces before comparing, so 'WEST ' = 'WEST' (also in IN, GROUP BY and joins). CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) values are stored and returned padded to n characters: 'AB' in a CHAR(4) column is 'AB '. LEN() ignores trailing spaces (TSQL-15). Leading spaces always count.
Spark: Spark compares strings exactly, so 'WEST ' <> 'WEST', and its string type never pads. A value read from a CHAR source column keeps whatever spaces it was stored with.
Fix: rtrim both sides of every text comparison, grouping and join key. Where the legacy output column is CHAR(n)/NCHAR(n), pad the value with rpad(x, n, ' ') (NULL stays NULL) so the output matches the stored legacy value. A CHAR(n) source column read into an expression keeps its padding (e.g. in + concatenation).
### TSQL-04: DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, not elapsed periods
Legacy: DATEDIFF(datepart, a, b) counts the datepart boundaries crossed between a and b: DATEDIFF(year, '2025-12-31', '2026-01-01') = 1 and DATEDIFF(month, '2025-01-31', '2025-02-01') = 1. DATEDIFF(week, ...) counts Sundays crossed, whatever SET DATEFIRST says. DATEDIFF(day, ...) on DATE values equals the day difference.
Spark: datediff(end, start) counts days (arguments reversed); months_between returns a fraction with its own month-end rule; floor(months/12) counts elapsed years, not boundaries.
Fix: year: year(b) - year(a). quarter: (year(b)*4 + quarter(b)) - (year(a)*4 + quarter(a)). month: (year(b)*12 + month(b)) - (year(a)*12 + month(a)). week: the difference of Sunday-anchored week numbers, floor(datediff(x, DATE'1899-12-31') / 7) for b minus a. day: datediff(b, a). Mind the argument order: T-SQL is (part, start, end), Spark's datediff is (end, start).
### TSQL-05: + concatenation with NULL yields NULL
Legacy: With CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL ON (the default), 'A' + NULL is NULL, so a whole concatenation is NULL when any part is. CONCAT() and CONCAT_WS() treat NULL as empty.
Spark: Spark's + is arithmetic only; concat() returns NULL when any argument is NULL, while concat_ws() skips NULLs and format_string writes 'null'.
Fix: Translate T-SQL + on strings to F.concat(...) (NULL if any part is NULL). Translate T-SQL CONCAT() to concat of coalesce(x, '') parts, and CONCAT_WS to concat_ws. CHAR(n) parts keep their padding inside the concatenation (TSQL-02).
### TSQL-13: Temp tables
Legacy: #temp tables hold intermediate results for the session.
Spark: Intermediate results are DataFrames or temporary views.
Fix: Make each #temp table a DataFrame (or temp view). Keep its column types: SELECT INTO creates columns with the source expressions' types, which can matter downstream.
### TSQL-15: LEN ignores trailing spaces; SUBSTRING from 0; LEFT and RIGHT
Legacy: LEN(x) does not count trailing spaces (DATALENGTH does). SUBSTRING(x, 0, n) returns n-1 characters, because position 0 is before the string. LEFT/RIGHT count characters.
Spark: length() counts trailing spaces; substring(x, 0, n) is treated like position 1 and returns n characters.
Fix: LEN(x) is length(rtrim(x)). SUBSTRING(x, s, n) with s < 1 returns substring(x, 1, n + s - 1) (empty if that is <= 0). Keep LEFT/RIGHT as substring with explicit positions.
### TSQL-16: CONVERT style codes
Legacy: CONVERT(type, date, style) formats dates by style: 101 mm/dd/yyyy, 103 dd/mm/yyyy, 104 dd.mm.yyyy, 105 dd-mm-yyyy, 106 dd mon yyyy, 111 yyyy/mm/dd, 112 yyyymmdd, 120 yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss, 121 with milliseconds, 23 yyyy-mm-dd. ### TSQL-19: Text ordering under collations (accents, case) in ORDER BY, MIN, MAX and rankings
Legacy: Under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text sorts case-insensitively with accent rules (Á sorts with A); MIN/MAX on text and ORDER BY text in a ranking follow that order.

"""T04 usp_build_claims_summary: migrated from estate/tsql/T04_usp_build_claims_summary.sql.

Legacy SHA-256: 632841c99f0c5919975c6fd2266ab04b33e1ba87424c55bbfbe7b0223f3bc975
Written by: LANSH translator (Claude)
Traps handled: TSQL-01, TSQL-02, TSQL-04, TSQL-05, TSQL-13, TSQL-16
Bugs reproduced on purpose (# LANSH-DEFECT): payment/reserve join fan-out inflates total_paid and incurred
"""
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession, Window
import pyspark.sql.functions as F


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    claims = inputs["stg.claims"]
    payments = inputs["stg.claim_payments"]
    reserves = inputs["stg.claim_reserves"]
    snapshots = inputs["stg.policy_snapshots"]

    as_of = F.to_date(F.lit(params["AsOfDate"]))

    # TSQL-13: #open_claims -> DataFrame (lines 63-74)
    # TSQL-01 / TSQL-02: status IN (...) ignores case and trailing spaces under the CI collation
    open_claims = (
        claims
        .where(
            F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("status"))).isin("OPEN", "REOPENED")
            & (F.col("reported_date") <= as_of)
        )
        .select(
            F.col("claim_id"),
            F.col("claim_number"),
            F.col("policy_id"),
            F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("lob_code"))).alias("lob_code"),
            F.col("status"),
            F.col("handler_code"),
            F.col("loss_date"),
            F.col("reported_date"),
        )
    )

    oc_ids = open_claims.select("claim_id")

    # TSQL-13: #reserve -> DataFrame (lines 83-95)
    # TSQL-01 / TSQL-02: PARTITION BY reserve_type puts case / trailing-space variants together
    w_res = (
        Window.partitionBy(F.col("claim_id"), F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("reserve_type"))))
        .orderBy(F.col("reserve_date").desc(), F.col("reserve_id").desc(), F.col("_row_seq").asc())
    )
    reserve = (
        reserves
        .where(F.col("reserve_date") <= as_of)
        .join(oc_ids, on="claim_id", how="inner")
        .withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w_res))
        .where(F.col("rn") == 1)
        .select("claim_id", "reserve_type", "reserve_amount")
    )

    # TSQL-13: #money -> DataFrame (lines 103-115)
    pay = (
        payments
        .where(F.col("payment_date") <= as_of)
        .select(F.col("claim_id").alias("p_claim_id"), F.col("payment_id"), F.col("amount"))
    )
    rsv = reserve.select(
        F.col("claim_id").alias("r_claim_id"), F.col("reserve_type"), F.col("reserve_amount")
    )
    rtype = F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("reserve_type")))  # TSQL-01 / TSQL-02 on lines 106-107
    money = (
        oc_ids
        .join(pay, F.col("claim_id") == F.col("p_claim_id"), "left")
        .join(rsv, F.col("claim_id") == F.col("r_claim_id"), "left")  # LANSH-DEFECT: payments x reserve rows fan-out before GROUP BY
        .groupBy("claim_id")
        .agg(
            F.countDistinct(F.col("payment_id")).alias("n_payments"),
            F.coalesce(F.sum(F.col("amount")), F.lit(0)).alias("total_paid"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: SUM counts each payment once per reserve row
            F.coalesce(
                F.max(F.when(rtype == "INDEMNITY", F.col("reserve_amount"))), F.lit(0)
            ).alias("indemnity_reserve"),
            F.coalesce(
                F.max(F.when(rtype == "EXPENSE", F.col("reserve_amount"))), F.lit(0)
            ).alias("expense_reserve"),
        )
    )

    # @snapshot_date = MAX(snapshot_date) <= @AsOfDate (lines 121-123); NULL matches nothing
    snap = (
        snapshots
        .where(F.col("snapshot_date") <= as_of)
        .agg(F.max(F.col("snapshot_date")).alias("snap_date"))
    )
    ps = (
        snapshots
        .join(snap, F.col("snapshot_date") == F.col("snap_date"), "inner")
        .select(F.col("policy_id").alias("ps_policy_id"), F.col("policy_number"))
    )

    joined = (
        open_claims
        .join(money, on="claim_id", how="inner")
        .join(ps, F.col("policy_id") == F.col("ps_policy_id"), "left")
    )

    result = joined.select(
        F.col("claim_id"),
        F.col("claim_number"),
        # TSQL-05: '+' concatenation is NULL if any part (e.g. handler_code) is NULL
        F.concat(
            F.col("lob_code"), F.lit("/"), F.col("claim_number"), F.lit("/"), F.col("handler_code")
        ).alias("claim_ref"),
        F.col("policy_id"),
        F.col("policy_number"),
        F.col("lob_code"),
        F.col("status"),
        F.col("handler_code"),
        F.col("loss_date"),
        # TSQL-16: CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), d, 103) -> dd/MM/yyyy
        F.date_format(F.col("loss_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy").alias("loss_date_text"),
        F.col("reported_date"),
        # TSQL-16: CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) -> first 6 chars of yyyyMMdd; TSQL-02 CHAR(6) padding
        F.rpad(
            F.substring(F.date_format(F.col("reported_date"), "yyyyMMdd"), 1, 6), 6, " "
        ).alias("reported_period"),
        # TSQL-04: DATEDIFF(DAY, start, end) -> datediff(end, start)
        F.datediff(as_of, F.col("reported_date")).alias("days_open"),
        F.col("n_payments"),
        F.col("total_paid"),
        F.col("indemnity_reserve"),
        F.col("expense_reserve"),
        (F.col("indemnity_reserve") + F.col("expense_reserve")).alias("current_reserve"),
        (F.col("total_paid") + F.col("indemnity_reserve") + F.col("expense_reserve")).alias("incurred"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: incurred carries the fanned-out total_paid
        as_of.alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"rpt.claims_summary": result}

The migrated code used a binary F.col('status').isin(...), which dropped 49 case variants and 11 trailing-space variants (the case_split and trailing_space_split signatures). Those missing rows also explain the lower totals for claim_id, policy_id, days_open and n_payments. (2) loss_date_text differed on all 740 matched rows: CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), d, 103) is dd/mm/yyyy, but the migration used the pattern 'MM/dd/yyyy' (style 101), so day and month were swapped (legacy 08/02/2019, candidate 02/08/2019).

Removed the stray leading comment so the module docstring comes first. Everything else is unchanged, including the payments × reserves fan-out, which is reproduced on purpose and marked LANSH-DEFECT.
